note: XDRProof hazard registry: each hazard is a named way Stellar ledger readers break. Source of the design: research blueprint (2026-11-18). Checks: R replay probe, C conformance, L linter, G guide, V verify facts. In `test`, c-base/s-base step names are recipe steps: generated, reproducible ledgers that become corpus entries in B4; "todo" marks placements not built yet; "planned" marks later stages.

hazards.title: An auth entry's signature does not cover its own bytes: a CREATE_CONTRACT_HOST_FN invocation is hashed in its V2 rendering
hazards.evidence: soroban-env-host auth.rs as stellar-core v30 links it (30.0.0 @6e6c4a87 for protocol 30, 28.0.0 @ba37ea5f for protocol 28; same code at lines 778, 803 and 2641): from_xdr reads SOROBAN_AUTHORIZED_FUNCTION_TYPE_CREATE_CONTRACT_HOST_FN into CreateContractArgsV2 with empty constructor arguments, to_xdr writes CREATE_CONTRACT_V2_HOST_FN, and get_signature_payload hashes root_invocation_to_xdr. Measured on stellar-core v30 at protocols 28 and 30: a v1 entry signed over its own bytes (as js-stellar-base authorizeEntry signs it) fails ed25519 verification; the same entry with a signature over the V2 rendering creates the contract. Signers, and readers that verify signatures from the entry bytes, get v1 creates wrong.
hazards.test: s-base `create-contract-v1-auth-signed-over-own-bytes` (fails) and `create-contract-v1-auth-signed-over-v2-rendering` (succeeds)
